what_happened: In job 4zcq, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The reading covered several things: a producer that hits its deadline, verifier-stage timeouts (criterion 3), and multi-part planning (criterion 4). The user narrowed it to the producer stage only and dropped criteria 3 and 4. Verifier timeouts were called rare, since verifiers cite recorded checks. Multi-part planning was called unrelated. What stays: a producer that hits its deadline keeps its worktree edits and a progress note. The job is recorded as timed out, not failed. `athena retry` resumes from the kept work and the note. Status shows timed out apart from failed.
cause: The reading stage turns a request's theme (deadline handling) into criteria for every stage and neighbouring topic it touches. It has no rule to scope a reading to the one stage whose failure the request is about, and no size check against what one producer run can finish before its fixed deadline. The reading also doesn't check whether each criterion is needed for the stated outcome, or how often the failure it covers occurs. So the user has to cut the scope after the reading is built.
prevention: Add a scope step to the reading stage. For each criterion it must name the stage or failure that the request's own words point to, and mark as out of scope any criterion about another stage or an unrelated capability. It should also estimate whether the criteria fit one producer run. Where a request touches several stages, the reading should keep the one stage named in the request and list the others as follow-up requests, not as criteria. A code check can flag a reading with more than a set number of criteria, or with criteria about more than one pipeline stage, before it is accepted.
proposed_request: Make a producer that reaches its fixed deadline recoverable. Scope: the producer stage only. Do not change verifier timeout handling or multi-part planning. Outcomes: (1) When the producer hits its deadline, it keeps its worktree edits and writes a progress note. (2) The job is recorded as timed out, not failed. (3) `athena retry` on a timed-out job resumes from the kept work and gives the producer the note. (4) `athena status` shows timed out as distinct from failed. Acceptance: a test with a producer stub that runs past the deadline shows the edits and the note are kept, the recorded state is timed out, retry starts from the kept work with the note, and status prints the two states differently. Existing failure paths for jobs that fail for other reasons are unchanged.
